copyright: The Atlantic Forest, Brazil (© FG Trade/Getty Images)
description: The Atlantic Forest is one of the world's great biodiversity hotspots, stretching along much of Brazil's Atlantic coast and into Argentina and Paraguay. Its landscape includes tropical and subtropical forests, mangroves and coastal habitats, providing a home for around 20,000 plant species and an extraordinary variety of wildlife, including jaguars and golden lion tamarins. Much of the forest has disappeared over the centuries, but it continues to play an important role in storing carbon and providing fresh water for millions of people across the region.

copyright: Aerial view of Rose Island, The Bahamas (© Abstract Aerial Art/Getty Images)
description: Rose Island is a picture-perfect escape in The Bahamas, where lush greenery meets some of the most vibrant blue waters in the Caribbean. Located just a short boat ride from Nassau, this peaceful cay is known for its pristine beaches, crystal-clear shallows and relaxed island atmosphere. Movie fans may recognize it as a filming location from the 1965 James Bond adventure Thunderball, but today Rose Island's biggest attractions are its natural beauty and unique wildlife, including its famous swimming pigs. Viewed from above, the island showcases the dazzling colours that make The Bahamas world-renowned, with turquoise lagoons, sandy shoals and clear waters creating a breathtaking tropical landscape.

copyright: Historic district of Triana, Seville, Spain (© Andrzej Rostek/Getty Images)
description: Cross the Guadalquivir River and discover Triana, one of Seville’s most vibrant neighbourhoods. Connected to the city’s historic centre by the iconic Triana Bridge since the 19th century, this riverside district is known for its colourful ceramics, flamenco heritage and lively local culture. Brightly decorated buildings, traditional tile workshops and bustling markets give Triana a character all its own. Stroll along Calle Betis for scenic river views, explore streets lined with artisan studios, or simply soak up the neighbourhood’s welcoming atmosphere. While Seville’s famous landmarks are just steps away, Triana offers a unique glimpse into the traditions, creativity and everyday life that help define Andalusia.

copyright: Lanterns for Diwali, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India (© Dinodia Photo/Getty Images)
description: Diwali, the Festival of Lights, is celebrated by millions of people around the world, including vibrant communities across Canada. Rooted in the Sanskrit word dipavali, meaning “row of lights,” the festival symbolizes the triumph of light over darkness and hope over adversity. Families and friends gather to light diyas and lanterns, create colourful rangoli, share sweets and take part in prayers and celebrations. While traditions vary across regions and faiths, Diwali is widely recognized as a time of reflection, gratitude and togetherness. As communities across Canada come together to celebrate, the festival continues to brighten neighbourhoods, workplaces and schools with its message of unity, joy and renewal.

copyright: A bison in the grasslands of Theodore Roosevelt National Park, North Dakota, USA (© Tandem Stock/Adobe Stock)
description: One of North America's most remarkable animals, the bison is a powerful symbol of strength, resilience and conservation. Weighing as much as 900 kilograms (2,000 pounds) and capable of running up to 55 km/h (35 mph), bison are surprisingly agile. Despite being commonly called buffalo, American bison are a distinct species known for their massive shoulder hump, curved horns and shaggy coats that help them thrive through harsh winters. Once pushed to the brink of extinction, bison have made an inspiring comeback thanks to conservation efforts across Canada and the United States, making them a powerful example of successful wildlife recovery.

copyright: Bamboo forest, Pīpīwai Trail, Haleakalā National Park, Maui, Hawaii, USA (© MNStudio/Getty Images)
description: Haleakalā National Park on Maui is home to an extraordinary mix of landscapes, from volcanic slopes and rainforest to towering bamboo forests. The park stretches from the summit of Haleakalā, which rises 3,055 metres above sea level, to the Pacific coast. More than 850 plant species grow here, including some found nowhere else on Earth, alongside native Hawaiian wildlife. One of the park's most popular walks is the Pīpīwai Trail, which winds through lush forest before reaching a remarkable bamboo grove. As the bamboo sways in the breeze, its tall stalks create distinctive sounds that add to the unique experience.

copyright: Wooden stile at a stone wall, Black Crag, Lake District, England (© Alex Treadway/Getty Images)
description: A simple wooden gate opens onto the Lake District, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in north-west England known for its lakes, rolling hills and centuries-old stone walls. This path leads toward Black Crag, the summit of Black Fell, which rises to about 323 metres and offers impressive views of Windermere, Coniston Water, and the Langdale Pikes. The route passes Tarn Hows, one of the region's most scenic spots, before climbing through a landscape shaped by nature and farming traditions. Some trails also follow Tom Gill, where woodland paths run alongside cascading waterfalls in this picturesque corner of Cumbria.
